sections.h2: What should I know about selling a house in Edmonds, WA?
sections.html:
Edmonds is a Puget Sound waterfront city in southwest Snohomish County, about 15 miles north of Seattle, and the population is older than most Puget Sound suburbs. The Census Bureau estimates 42,748 residents as of July 1, 2025, close to the 42,853 counted in 2020, so the city has barely grown in five years.

That profile shapes who sells and why. Nearly a quarter of residents are 65 or older, 70.9 percent of homes are owner-occupied and 88.2 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Typical sale triggers are downsizing, an inherited house, a move closer to family and rental properties that owners want to exit. Each of those carries its own paperwork, which the sections below walk through. Edmonds also has about five miles of Puget Sound shoreline and a regional arts scene downtown, which keeps buyers interested in close-in homes.

sections.h2: How does Edmonds geography affect a house sale?
sections.html:
Edmonds is a set of hillside neighborhoods around a downtown valley, so location inside the city matters to buyers. It was platted in 1884 and incorporated on August 14, 1890, making it the oldest incorporated city in Snohomish County. Early work was in shingle mills and logging, and the hills around the downtown valley were built out as suburbs from the 1950s on and later annexed. The result is a city of distinct pockets:

  • Downtown and the Bowl: a valley with views of Puget Sound and the Olympic Mountains, close to the beach, the fishing pier and the ferry dock.
  • Five Corners, Firdale, Perrinville, Seaview, Sherwood and Westgate: hillside neighborhoods, several with their own small commercial centers.
  • The State Route 99 corridor: the eastern commercial edge, home to the city's car dealerships.
  • Esperance: an unincorporated enclave in the southeast corner that has resisted annexation, so confirm whether an address is inside city limits.

Transportation is a selling point. The Washington State Ferries route runs to Kingston, the downtown station is served by Amtrak and Sounder, and Community Transit buses reach outlying areas. Only about 11.7 percent of residents work inside the city, and about 11 percent commute to Seattle, which is why buyers ask about transit and drive times first.

sections.h2: Do Edmonds landlords need a license, and what about backyard units?
sections.html:
Yes. The City of Edmonds requires a business license for any business operating in the city, including property owners, and it places home rentals in the General Business License category. The city page lists a $186.87 application fee and a $74.75 annual renewal. Applications run through the state Business Licensing Service on the Department of Revenue website, and the city follows up for a floor plan and supplemental questionnaire. Business Licensing can be reached at 425-775-2525.

A landlord selling a tenant-occupied house should confirm the license is current and tell the buyer what the lease says. For building questions, the Planning and Development Department is at 121 5th Ave N, phone 425-771-0220. The city runs a Pre-Approved DADU Plan Program for detached accessory dwelling units, though its page says no plans are in the catalog yet, so any existing backyard unit should come with permit records. The department's posted counter hours since September 2, 2025 are Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 3 p.m., closed Wednesdays, with phone and digital help weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Confirm hours before you visit.

  • Gather permit and inspection records for additions, decks and converted space.
  • Keep the rental license, lease copies and security deposit ledger together for the buyer.
  • Ask the department how to confirm an unpermitted structure before it surprises a buyer's inspector.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell an Edmonds house quickly?
sections.html:
Three routes cover most Edmonds situations, and the choice turns on condition, timeline and how much preparation you want to do.

  • A traditional listing: strong demand for views and walkable streets, but staging, showings and financing contingencies take time.
  • A direct sale to an investor or cash buyer: useful for dated houses, estate sales and tenant-occupied homes, with fewer repairs requested and a flexible closing date.
  • A for-sale-by-owner sale: you keep the agent fee but carry the disclosure, negotiation and paperwork.

For an estate sale, ask the probate attorney whether the personal representative has the authority to sign before you accept an offer. For every route, compare offers by what you keep after the excise tax, any liens and the mortgage payoff.

sections.h2: What disclosures and excise tax come with an Edmonds sale?
sections.html:
For improved residential property, RCW 64.06.020 requires the seller to deliver a completed disclosure statement unless the buyer waived it or the transfer is exempt. Delivery is due within five business days of mutual acceptance unless the parties agree otherwise, and the buyer then has three business days to rescind. The form asks about title, water, sewer, structural issues and more, and it says to write NA rather than leave blanks.

The real estate excise tax is owed on the date of sale, which the Department of Revenue ties to the date the deed is signed before the notary, whatever the recording date. If the tax is not paid within one month, interest is charged from the date of sale, and the 2026 rate is 6 percent. Keep your sale records for at least four years, because the state can audit a sale and ask for support of the price or any exemption.

sections.h2: How do Snohomish County property taxes work for an Edmonds seller?
sections.html:
Snohomish County collects property tax in two installments, April 30 and October 31, and a statement should reach owners by March 15 under RCW 84.56.020. The October 31, 2026 second-half date has passed, so confirm it was paid. The next due date is April 30, 2027.

The county treasurer advises owners with a mortgage escrow to read escrow statements closely, since a payment collected at a refinance may not reach the treasurer until April or October. Mailed payments only need a postmark by the due date. Residential parcels with four or fewer units pay 9 percent annual interest on late taxes and no added penalty. The excise tax counter at the treasurer's office is open weekdays from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.

faqs.q: What is the population of Edmonds, WA?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 42,748 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census count was 42,853.

faqs.q: Do I need a business license to rent out a house in Edmonds?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of Edmonds treats home rentals as a General Business License, with a $186.87 application fee and a $74.75 annual renewal, filed through the state Department of Revenue system. Call Edmonds Business Licensing at 425-775-2525 with questions.

faqs.q: How long does an Edmonds seller have to give the buyer a disclosure statement?
faqs.a: Within five business days after mutual acceptance of the contract, unless the parties agree otherwise. The buyer then has three business days after delivery to rescind, under RCW 64.06.020. A buyer can waive the right to receive the form.

faqs.q: When is the Washington excise tax due on an Edmonds sale?
faqs.a: On the date of sale, paid to the county treasurer, with interest charged if it is not paid within one month. The state tiers start at 1.1 percent and rise to 1.28 percent above $525,000, plus a local rate. Sales beginning January 1, 2027 shift the first tier to $551,000.

No. Esperance is an unincorporated area in the southeast corner that sits surrounded by Edmonds and has resisted annexation. Ask the county which jurisdiction handles permits and taxes for the address.
